name.text: AROC of a quadratic over an interval (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
The graph below shows the quadratic \[ f(x) = {@fx@}. \]

The points \(A\) and \(B\) lie on the curve, at \(x = {@pp@}\) and \(x = {@qq@}\). The straight line joining them is the secant line \(AB\).

Find the average rate of change of \(f\) from \(x = {@pp@}\) to \(x = {@qq@}\). You may read the coordinates of \(A\) and \(B\) from the graph, or evaluate \(f\) yourself. Give an exact value (an integer or a simple fraction).

[[jsxgraph width="470px" height="420px"]] var b = {#bb#}, c = {#cc#}; var p = {#pp#}, q = {#qq#}; var fp = {#fp#}, fq = {#fq#}; function f(x){ return x*x + b*x + c; } /* Choose a window that comfortably contains A and B with padding. */ var xs = [p, q], ys = [fp, fq]; var xmin = Math.min.apply(null, xs), xmax = Math.max.apply(null, xs); var ymin = Math.min.apply(null, ys), ymax = Math.max.apply(null, ys); var xpad = Math.max(3, 0.35*(xmax - xmin) + 2); var ypad = Math.max(2.0, 0.35*(ymax - ymin) + 2); var bx0 = xmin - xpad, bx1 = xmax + xpad; var by0 = ymin - ypad, by1 = ymax + ypad; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [bx0, by1, bx1, by0], axis: true, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false, keepaspectratio: true, pan: {enabled:false}, zoom: {enabled:false} }); /* Draw the parabola across the FULL width of the board. With keepaspectratio the visible x-range can be wider than [bx0, bx1], so read the live board edges (getBoundingBox() = [xmin, ymax, xmax, ymin]) as the curve's x-limits. */ board.create('functiongraph', [f, function(){ return board.getBoundingBox()[0]; }, function(){ return board.getBoundingBox()[2]; } ], {strokeColor:'#1565c0', strokeWidth:2, highlight:false}); var A = board.create('point', [p, fp], {name:'A', size:3, fixed:true, fillColor:'#d32f2f', strokeColor:'#d32f2f', label:{offset:[-10,-14], anchorX:'right', anchorY:'top'}}); var B = board.create('point', [q, fq], {name:'B', size:3, fixed:true, fillColor:'#d32f2f', strokeColor:'#d32f2f', label:{offset:[10,12], anchorX:'left', anchorY:'bottom'}}); board.create('line', [A, B], {strokeColor:'#2e7d32', strokeWidth:2, straightFirst:true, straightLast:true, dash:0, highlight:false}); /* Coordinate labels placed as free text away from the curve so they are always readable. */ board.create('text', [p, fp, '(' + p + ', ' + fp + ')'], {anchorX:'right', anchorY:'top', offset:[-6,-6], fontSize:13, cssStyle:'color:#d32f2f', fixed:true}); board.create('text', [q, fq, '(' + q + ', ' + fq + ')'], {anchorX:'left', anchorY:'bottom', offset:[6,6], fontSize:13, cssStyle:'color:#d32f2f', fixed:true}); [[/jsxgraph]]
Average rate of change \( = \) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The average rate of change of \(f\) from \(x = {@pp@}\) to \(x = {@qq@}\) is the slope of the secant line \(AB\): the change in output divided by the change in input, \[ \text{AROC} = \frac{f({@qq@}) - f({@pp@})}{{@qq@} - {@pp@}}. \]

Evaluate \(f(x) = {@fx@}\) at the two endpoints:

\[ \begin{align*} f({@pp@}) &= ({@pp@})^2 + ({@bb@})({@pp@}) + ({@cc@}) = {@fp@}, \\ f({@qq@}) &= ({@qq@})^2 + ({@bb@})({@qq@}) + ({@cc@}) = {@fq@}. \end{align*} \]

So

\[ \text{AROC} = \frac{ {@fq@} - ({@fp@}) }{ {@qq@} - ({@pp@}) } = \frac{ {@fq-fp@} }{ {@qq-pp@} } = {@ta1@}. \]

Geometrically this is the slope of the green secant \(AB\). A positive value means \(f\) increases on average over the interval; a negative value means it decreases; a value of \(0\) means \(f\) ends at the same height it started, even though it is not constant in between.

node.description: Gave f(q)-f(p) only (did not divide by the run)?

truefeedback.text: That is the change in output, \(f(q)-f(p)\), on its own. The average rate of change is a slope: you still need to divide by the run, the change in input \(q-p\). Set it up as \(\dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}\) and divide.

Your value has the right size but the wrong sign. Keep the "later minus earlier" order the same on top and bottom: \(\dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}\). If you subtract \(f(p)-f(q)\) on top, you must also write \(p-q\) on the bottom — the two swaps cancel.

node.description: Averaged f(p) and f(q) instead of finding the rate?

truefeedback.text: It looks like you found the average of the two heights, \(\tfrac12\bigl(f(p)+f(q)\bigr)\). That is the middle \(y\)-value, not a rate. A rate of change compares the change in height to the change in \(x\): \(\dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}\), the slope of the secant \(AB\).

node.description: Inverted the ratio: run over rise (q-p)/(f(q)-f(p)) = 1/AROC?

truefeedback.text: You have divided the wrong way round: this is the run over the rise, \(\dfrac{q-p}{f(q)-f(p)}\). The average rate of change is rise over run — the change in height divided by the change in \(x\): \(\dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}\). Turn your fraction the other way up.

falsefeedback.text: Not correct. The average rate of change is the slope of the secant \(AB\): \(\dfrac{f(q)-f(p)}{q-p}\). Read \(f(p)\) and \(f(q)\) off the graph (or evaluate \(f\)), find the change in height, and divide by the change in \(x\). Have another go — the worked solution appears after this attempt.

qtest.description: Forgot to divide by the run: f(q)-f(p)
